chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said:

I was present when Ibn Abi Layla judged in the case of a man who had assigned the usufruct (income/produce) of his house to one of his relatives but did not specify a time limit. The man died, and his heirs came to Ibn Abi Layla, and the relative who had been assigned the house also came. Ibn Abi Layla said: 'I see that I should leave it as the owner left it.'
Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafi said to him: 'By Allah, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) has judged in this mosque contrary to what you have judged.'

He said: 'And what is your knowledge?' He said: 'I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) saying: "Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) judged in the return of the usufruct and the execution of the inheritance."'
Ibn Abi Layla said: 'Is this in your book?' He said: 'Yes.'
He said: 'Then send for it and bring it to me.' Muhammad ibn Muslim said: 'On the condition that you do not look in the book except for that hadith.' He said: 'That is for you.'
So he showed him the hadith from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in the book, and he reversed his judgment.

key_terms.اَلْحَبِيس: The confined or restricted portion (here referring to the restricted usufruct)
key_terms.غَلَّة: Usufruct or produce/income derived from property
key_terms.قَضَى: Judged or issued a legal ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on a bequest of property usufruct without a specified time limit?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the jurisprudential debate over indefinite usufruct bequests (*ghallah*), contrasting the initial ruling of Ibn Abi Layla with the authoritative precedent of Imam Ali (AS) as transmitted by Imam al-Baqir (AS). It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on returning the usufruct to the general estate for full inheritance distribution rather than allowing perpetual private benefit, a principle validated here through the rigorous chain of transmission (*isnad*) and the judge's acceptance of the written record (*kitab*).
